title: Geopolitical Conflict & Wartime Financial Contagion Simulation
description: An interactive macro-economic and financial asset simulation modeling how the outbreak and escalation of war impact equities, commodities, safe-haven flows, sector divergences, and market volatility.

components.description: Multi-series time-series comparison chart tracking S&P 500, Defense ETF, Brent Crude Oil, and Gold over 52 weeks of conflict.
Interactive grid displaying percentage returns across 6 key market sectors: Aerospace & Defense, Energy, Commercial Aviation, Tech Growth, Consumer Staples, and Sovereign Bonds.
Dynamic animated particle flow showing capital liquidating from high-beta equities and streaming into Gold, US Dollar (DXY), and 10Y Treasuries.
Circular fear/greed volatility gauge showing market panic intensity from Calm (<15) to Extreme Panic (>40).

interactive_controls.label: Conflict Escalation Level
interactive_controls.unit: Stage (0: Peace, 1: Tension, 2: Conventional War, 3: Total Blockade)

educational_cards.title: Flight to Safety & Capital Migration
educational_cards.content: During wartime escalation, asset managers rapidly de-risk portfolios. Capital flees equity risk premiums into sovereign balance sheets (US 10-Year Treasuries), physical gold reserves, and reserve currencies (USD, CHF).

educational_cards.title: The Energy Supply Chokepoint & Stagflation
educational_cards.content: Modern warfare disproportionately weaponizes energy straits (Strait of Hormuz, Bab-el-Mandeb, pipelines). Spikes in crude oil increase input costs across all industries, creating cost-push stagflation that ties central banks' hands.

educational_cards.title: Asymmetric Sector Divergence
educational_cards.content: While broad indices fall, Aerospace & Defense primes (missile systems, ammunition, surveillance) experience secular budget re-ratings (+30-70%), while airlines and consumer discretionary face collapsing operating margins.

educational_cards.title: Historical War Cycles: Initial Panic vs. 12-Month Rebound
educational_cards.content: Empirical market history (1973 Yom Kippur, 1990 Desert Storm, 2003 Iraq) demonstrates that broad equities typically bottom within 3 to 6 weeks of initial kinetic action, often recovering pre-war valuations within 12 months as uncertainty resolves.
